rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an aging heat treatment to form nanoprecipitates, whereas the paper used cold rolling and subsequent annealing. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (thermal precipitation vs. mechanical deformation plus recovery/recrystallization).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies an aging temperature below recrystallization and room-temperature tensile tests. The paper used room-temperature cold rolling and annealing at 650–800 °C, with room-temperature tensile testing. The testing environment (room-temperature tension) matches, but the processing conditions (aging vs. rolling+annealing) are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes precipitation strengthening from coherent nanoprecipitates. The paper's mechanism relies on work hardening, dislocation accumulation, texture, and solid-solution strengthening from cold rolling, followed by recovery and recrystallization upon annealing. These are different classes of strengthening mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved strength and ductility relative to the as-cast baseline. The paper found that cold rolling increased strength but decreased ductility, and annealing decreased strength but increased ductility; it did not report a simultaneous improvement in both properties from a single intervention.
